--- title: "3.10 Bonus: Tables & Plots of Results" --- - Most every quantitative publication should include a descriptive statistics table and a table and/or plot of model results - Sometimes in the main text, sometimes in the Online Appendix - Stata and R can automate these tables and plots of results - [Tables]{.underline} - Stata - [**desctable**](/software/desctable/index.qmd) or [**dtable**](https://www.stata.com/links/stata-basics/create-descriptive-tables-with-dtable/) for descriptive statistics - [**esttab**](https://repec.sowi.unibe.ch/stata/estout/esttab.html) for model results - R - **modelsummary** package - [**datasummary**](https://modelsummary.com/vignettes/datasummary.html) function for descriptive statistics - [**modelsummary**](https://modelsummary.com/vignettes/modelsummary.html) function for model results - [Plots of model results]{.underline} - Stata - [**coefplot**](https://repec.sowi.unibe.ch/stata/coefplot/getting-started.html) - R - **modelsummary** package's [**modelplot**](https://modelsummary.com/vignettes/modelplot.html) function The examples use the GSS marijuana legalization data from [3.5](3-5-predictions.qmd#gss-example-marijuana-legalization), with three models that add IVs step by step: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss22", clear (GSS 1972-2022 CDA - Categorical Data Analysis | 2024-12-03) . . drop if missing(grass, age, conserv, faminc, college, woman, race4) (37,924 observations deleted) . recode grass 2 = 0 (0 changes made to grass) . lab def glab 0"not be legal" 1 "should be legal" . lab val grass glab . . * Create year since 1975 variable . gen year1975 = year - 1975 . lab var year1975 "years since 1975" . . // stepwise binary logit model, storing each time // . qui logit grass c.age c.year1975##c.year1975, or . est store mjmod1 . * mecompare without a varlist estimates AMEs for all IVs. . ** Add store() option to save MEs to make a table or plot . qui mecompare, amount(sd) store(mes1) model(mjmod1) . . qui logit grass c.age c.year1975##c.year1975 i.conserv, or . est store mjmod2 . qui mecompare, amount(sd) store(mes2) model(mjmod2) . . qui logit grass c.age c.year1975##c.year1975 i.conserv /// > c.faminc i.degree i.woman i.race4, or . est store mjmod3 . qui mecompare, amount(sd) store(mes3) model(mjmod3) ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(haven) # import Stata data and labels library(dplyr) # data manipulation library(ggplot2) # graphs library(modelsummary) # tables and plots of results library(marginaleffects) # predictions and marginal effects library(cleanplots) # graph scheme cleanplots_defaults() # Center changes in continuous IVs on each observation's value options(marginaleffects_contrast_direction = "center") gss <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss22.dta") # Drop any missing data on model vars gss <- gss[complete.cases(gss[c("grass", "age", "conserv", "faminc", "college", "woman", "race4")]), ] # Create year since 1975 variable; treat binary/nominal variables as factors gss <- gss |> mutate(year1975 = as.numeric(year) - 1975, conserv = as_factor(conserv), degree = as_factor(degree), woman = as_factor(woman), race4 = as_factor(race4)) |> droplevels() # stepwise binary logit model, storing each time mjmod1 <- glm(grass ~ age + poly(year1975, 2, raw = TRUE), data = gss, family = binomial(link = "logit")) mjmod2 <- glm(grass ~ age + poly(year1975, 2, raw = TRUE) + conserv, data = gss, family = binomial(link = "logit")) mjmod3 <- glm(grass ~ age + poly(year1975, 2, raw = TRUE) + conserv + faminc + degree + woman + race4, data = gss, family = binomial(link = "logit")) ``` ::: ::: ## Tables of odds ratios - Tables of odds ratios are traditional and should generally be included somewhere - I usually include these in the Online Appendix - With **esttab**, use option **eform** (exponentiate) to get odds ratios ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . * Use esttab to make single table of ORs . esttab mjmod1 mjmod2 mjmod3, /// > eform nobase b(3) se(3) nogaps label varwidth(35) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > --- (1) (2) (3) > should mar~l should mar~l should mar~l > -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > --- should marijuana be made legal > age of respondent 0.976*** 0.978*** 0.976 > *** (0.001) (0.001) (0.001) > years since 1975 0.956*** 0.958*** 0.957 > *** (0.003) (0.003) (0.003) > years since 1975 # years since 1975 1.002*** 1.002*** 1.002 > *** (0.000) (0.000) (0.000) > Conservative 0.467*** 0.433 > *** (0.013) (0.012) > Family Income in 1000s 0.999 > (0.000) > high school 1.274 > *** (0.049) > associate/junior college 1.435 > *** (0.085) > bachelor's 1.583 > *** (0.075) > graduate 1.782 > *** (0.102) > Women 0.669 > *** (0.017) > Black 0.856 > *** (0.033) > Other 0.510 > *** (0.036) > Hispanic 0.438 > *** (0.025) > -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > --- Observations 34466 34466 34466 > -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > --- Exponentiated coefficients; Standard errors in parentheses * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001 ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} modelsummary(list("Model 1" = mjmod1, "Model 2" = mjmod2, "Model 3" = mjmod3), exponentiate = TRUE, fmt = 3, stars = c("*" = .05, "**" = .01, "***" = .001), coef_rename = TRUE, gof_map = "nobs") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: - Default is to show table within Stata/R, can export to Word (.rtf or .docx), Excel, LaTeX, etc. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```stata * Use .rtf format to export to Word esttab mjmod1 mjmod2 mjmod3 using or_table.rtf, replace /// eform nobase b(3) se(3) nogaps label varwidth(35) ``` ## R ```r modelsummary(list("(1)" = mjmod1, "(2)" = mjmod2, "(3)" = mjmod3), exponentiate = TRUE, fmt = 3, stars = c("*" = .05, "**" = .01, "***" = .001), coef_rename = TRUE, gof_map = "nobs", output = "mjmods_or.docx") ``` ::: ## Tables of marginal effects - In Stata, use [**mecompare** -- see "plotting and tabulating results"](/software/mecompare/index.qmd) - **mecompare** without a variable list will calculate AMEs for all IVs in the model - I always add **amount(sd)** so all continuous IVs are a +SD effect - Option **store(*sname*)** will save the MEs; *sname* is your name for what they are called - Also pass the stored **model(*mname*)** - Stored MEs are named *sname_mname* - Use **esttab** to make the table - In R, use [**avg_comparisons**](https://marginaleffects.com/man/r/comparisons.html) and list all IVs in a **variables = list()** option - Save each call as an object - Use **modelsummary** to make the table - Note my **shape** option which is needed here ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . * Use esttab to make a single table of MEs. . ** mecompare saves them as the store() name _ model() name . esttab mes1_mjmod1 mes2_mjmod2 mes3_mjmod3, /// > b(3) se(3) nogaps label varwidth(32) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- (1) (2) (3) should mar~l should mar~l should mar~l -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- age + SD (centered) -0.080*** -0.073*** -0.076*** (0.002) (0.002) (0.002) year1975 + SD (centered) 0.155*** 0.154*** 0.157*** (0.002) (0.002) (0.002) Conservative - Not Conservative -0.143*** -0.153*** (0.005) (0.005) faminc + SD (centered) -0.003 (0.003) high school - less than high sch 0.044*** (0.007) associate/junio - less than high 0.067*** (0.011) bachelor's - less than high scho 0.086*** (0.009) graduate - less than high school 0.109*** (0.011) Women - Men -0.075*** (0.005) Black - White -0.029*** (0.007) Other - White -0.117*** (0.011) Hispanic - White -0.140*** (0.008) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Observations 34466 34466 34466 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Standard errors in parentheses * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001 ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sd_age <- round(sd(gss$age), 2) sd_year <- round(sd(gss$year1975), 2) sd_inc <- round(sd(gss$faminc), 2) mes1 <- avg_comparisons(mjmod1, variables = list(age = sd_age, year1975 = sd_year)) mes2 <- avg_comparisons(mjmod2, variables = list(age = sd_age, year1975 = sd_year, conserv = "reference")) mes3 <- avg_comparisons(mjmod3, variables = list(age = sd_age, year1975 = sd_year, conserv = "reference", faminc = sd_inc, degree = "reference", woman = "reference", race4 = "reference")) modelsummary(list("Model 1" = mes1, "Model 2" = mes2, "Model 3" = mes3), shape = term : contrast ~ model, fmt = 3, stars = c("*" = .05, "**" = .01, "***" = .001), gof_map = "nobs") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note icon="false" appearance="simple"} [**esttab**](https://repec.sowi.unibe.ch/stata/estout/esttab.html) and [**modelsummary**](https://modelsummary.com/vignettes/modelsummary.html) have tons of customization options to produce publication-ready tables ::: ## Plots of marginal effects - You could plot the odds ratios, but I don't find it very informative and it can be problematic - Effect size is hard to understand - ORs rescale across models, so are not comparable / cannot be used to compare effect sizes across models - All continuous IVs are +1 effects, which are not comparable across IVs, and usually don't reflect much of that variable's effect - Marginal effects do not have these limitations, can be compared directly across models, and can be put in a meaningful unit of change (my default is to plot the +SD MEs for continuous IVs) - **2sd** or **trimrange** is also reasonable - Always include a reference line at 0 which indicates no effect ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . * Use coefplot. Add a xline(0) to show no effect . coefplot mes1_mjmod1 mes2_mjmod2 mes3_mjmod3, xline(0) /// > legend(order(2 "Model 1 " 4 "Model 2" 6 "Model 3")) /// > xtitle("ME on Pr(support legal)") graphregion(margin(l=10)) /// > title("[3.10.a] Average marginal effects from binary logit: Pr(supports ma > rijuana legalization)", span) ``` ![](fig/cda-03_10_a-coefplot-AMEs.png){width=80% fig-alt="Average marginal effects with confidence intervals from the three models: the effects of age and year change little across models, and conservatives, women, and Black, Other, and Hispanic adults are less supportive while more educated adults are more supportive."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} modelplot(list("Model 1" = mes1, "Model 2" = mes2, "Model 3" = mes3), shape = term : contrast ~ model) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) + scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) + labs(title = "[3.10.a] Average marginal effects from binary logit: Pr(supports marijuana legalization)", x = "ME on Pr(support legal)", color = NULL) + theme(plot.title.position = "plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3-10-tables-plots_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-alt='Average marginal effects with confidence intervals from the three models: the effects of age and year change little across models, and conservatives, women, and Black, Other, and Hispanic adults are less supportive while more educated adults are more supportive.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: - In Stata, can customize **coefplot**, e.g. with headings for nominal IVs ```{.stata-run} . * can customize coefplot, e.g. with headings for nominal IVs . coefplot mes1_mjmod1 mes2_mjmod2 mes3_mjmod3, /// > headings("high school - *" = "{bf:Education}" /// > "Black - *" = "{bf:Race-Ethnicity}") /// > xline(0) legend(order(2 "Model 1 " 4 "Model 2" 6 "Model 3")) /// > xtitle("ME on Pr(support legal)") graphregion(margin(l=10)) /// > title("[3.10.b] Average marginal effects from binary logit: Pr(supports ma > rijuana legalization)", span) ``` ![](fig/cda-03_10_b-coefplot-AMEs.png){width=80% fig-alt="The same average marginal effects plot with headings that group the education and race-ethnicity contrasts."}
